interest: This document is notable as a State Department record documenting Japanese naval presence and flag-showing visits in Central American waters during the interwar period. It highlights local media reaction through an editorial in the Nicaraguan newspaper La Noticia, which commented on the arrival of the Japanese fleet at the exact time U.S. Navy planes were visiting Nicaragua on a flight from the Panama Canal Zone (Coco Solo) to San Diego. This juxtaposition illustrates regional awareness of and sensitivity toward U.S.-Japanese naval rivalry along the approaches to the Panama Canal.
overview: This file consists of a U.S. State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file 894.3317 (Visits Of Vessels And Aircraft Of Japan To Ports Of Nicaragua). The sheet records Despatch No. 1473 from Daniels in Nicaragua dated September 23, reporting on a visit of a Japanese naval fleet to Nicaraguan waters. The despatch transmitted an editorial from the Nicaraguan newspaper La Noticia commenting on the Japanese fleet visit taking place concurrently with a goodwill or transit flight of U.S. naval aircraft visiting Nicaragua on their way from Coco Solo in the Canal Zone to San Diego, cross-referenced to file 711.17/261.

The despatch reports on a visit of the Japanese fleet to Nicaraguan waters and transmits an editorial from the newspaper La Noticia dated September 23. The editorial discusses the Japanese fleet's presence occurring at the same time as a visit by U.S. naval aircraft en route from Coco Solo to San Diego, with a cross-reference noting 'SEE 711.17/261'.
